text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

London's May white sugar contract tumbled almost $6.00 on Monday with weakness blamed on pre-expiry book-squaring and the downward correction in New York. May last traded down $5.80 at $306.00 per tonne after a new bout of selling toward the close and August was down $2.00 at $308.80 per tonne, while the outer months also lost ground. Activity in London was dominated by the standard rolling of spot positions into further forward months with commission houses and other brokers featuring on both sides of the market.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended lower in a session dominated by heavy selling in the May/July switch, dealers said. The spot May contract bore the brunt of the day's losses, as speculators, eager to unwind positions ahead of the contract's expiry in two weeks rolled longs into the back months. Traders said views the market was substantially overbought after rallying recently to seven-month highs contributed to the weakness.

Spot May fell 0.09 cents/lb on the day to 11.24 cents/lb, having traded from 11.12 to 11.27 cents. July fell 0.03 cents/lb to 11.13 cents/lb, while the back months eased between 0.01 and 0.06 cents. Without constructive fundamental news, traders expect the pressure on May to continue for the next several sessions. Technically, light support for the May contract was seen at 11.08-11.10 and then at 10.80-10.90. To the upside, a significant hurdle awaited the market at last week's highs of 11.38.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports from third countries in February 1997 amounted to 99,561 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative imports in October/February 1996/97 up to 503,170 tonnes against 518,976 tonnes in October/February 1995/96. Major countries of origin in October/February 1996/97 were Mauritius with 236,481 tonnes raws against 297,733 tonnes, Guyana with 101,643 tonnes, up from 65,310 tonnes and Fiji with 79,900 tonnes compared to 85,180 tonnes.

Total imports from third countries in 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) reached 1.238 million tonnes. Sugar exports to third countries in February 1997 amounted to 22,576 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 89,723 tonnes against 99,456 tonnes in the corresponding year-ago period. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Israel with 37,399 tonnes whites against 32,906 tonnes, Norway with 17,151 tonnes, down from 19,466 tonnes and Hong Kong with 12,353 tonnes compared to 7,895 tonnes. Total exports to third countries in 1995/96 amounted to 324,415 tonnes.

SWITZERLAND - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 11,169 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 8,498 tonnes. Cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (October/February) were down at 51,128 tonnes compared to 64,717 tonnes in October/February 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 169,593 tonnes against 155,620 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/February 1996/97 were Germany with 35,278 tonnes whites against 40,627 tonnes and France with 9,608 tonnes compared to 17,055 tonnes.

JAMAICA - Sugar output in 1996/97 (November/October) is estimated at 246,000 tonnes, slightly down on earlier projections of 256,000 tonnes. However, the total is still up on the 1995/96 result of 238,000 tonnes and also well above the 211,000 tonnes attained in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in 1996/97 is estimated to rise only slightly to 126,000 tonnes compared to 125,300 tonnes in 1995/96 and 120,100 tonnes in 1994/95. Molasses output will fall off somewhat to 100,900 tonnes compared to 101,000 in 1995/96 and the 1994/95 result of 87,305 tonnes.
Sri Lanka reportedly bought one cargo of Mexican white sugar for first half June arrival at $337.98 per tonne CFFO.
